source.note: Official DBE November 2017 Mathematics P2 marking guidelines (English/Afrikaans). Bilingual PDF; English transcribed only.

extraction.method: transcription from the official PDF text layer, checked against 140 dpi page renders

notes: If a candidate answers a question TWICE, only mark the FIRST attempt. If a candidate has crossed out an attempt of a question and not redone the question, mark the crossed out version. Consistent accuracy applies in ALL aspects of the marking guidelines. Stop marking at the second calculation error. Assuming answers/values in order to solve a problem is NOT acceptable. A mark for a correct statement (a statement mark is independent of a reason) is indicated by S. A mark for a correct reason (a reason mark may only be awarded if the statement is correct) is indicated by R. Award a mark if the statement AND reason are both correct (S/R).

In $\Delta OVN$ and $\Delta OWS$:

$\hat{O}_2=\hat{O}_2$ [common]

$\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{V}}\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{W}}\mathrm{S}=90^{\circ}$ [from 10.1]

$\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{N}}\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{S}}\mathrm{W}$ [sum of $\angle$s in $\Delta$]

$\therefore\Delta OVN ||| \Delta OWS$ [$\angle$, $\angle$, $\angle$]

$\therefore\dfrac{VN}{WS}=\dfrac{ON}{OS}$

But $VN=\dfrac{1}{2}MN$ [given]

$\therefore\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}MN}{WS}=\dfrac{ON}{OS}$

$\therefore OS\cdot MN=2\,ON\cdot WS$

alternatives.label: OR
alternatives.working_md:
In $\Delta OVM$ and $\Delta OWS$:

$\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{V}}\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{W}}\mathrm{S}=90^{\circ}$ [from 10.1]

$\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{M}}\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{O}\hat{\mathrm{S}}\mathrm{W}$ [sum of $\angle$s in $\Delta$]

$\Delta OVM ||| \Delta OWS$ [$\angle$, $\angle$, $\angle$]

$\dfrac{OM}{OS}=\dfrac{VM}{WS}$

$VN=\dfrac{1}{2}MN$ [given], so $\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}MN}{WS}=\dfrac{OM}{OS}$

$\therefore OS\cdot MN=2\,ON\cdot WS$ [$VM=VN$].

alternatives.label: OR
alternatives.working_md:
If any other two triangles are used, first prove $TW=WS$ by proving $\Delta OWT\equiv\Delta OWS$.

In $\Delta OVM$ and $\Delta OWT$: $\Delta OVM ||| \Delta OWT$ [$\angle$, $\angle$, $\angle$].

$\dfrac{VM}{WT}=\dfrac{OM}{OT}$

$VN=VM=\dfrac{1}{2}MN$ [given], and $WT=WS$, $OT=OS$ [$\Delta OWT\equiv\Delta OWS$].

$\therefore\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}MN}{WS}=\dfrac{ON}{OS}$, so $OS\cdot MN=2\,ON\cdot WS$.

$\dfrac{AD}{AC}=\dfrac{AB}{AD}$ [similar $\Delta$s]

$AB=r$ and $BC=2r$, so $AC=3r$.

In $\Delta ACE$: $\tan\hat{E}=\dfrac{AC}{AE}=\dfrac{3r}{\sqrt{3}\,r}=\sqrt{3}$, so $\hat{E}=60^{\circ}$.

$\therefore\hat{D}_1=60^{\circ}$ [from 11.2.2(a)] and $\hat{A}_1=60^{\circ}$ [$\angle$s of $\Delta=180^{\circ}$].

$\therefore\Delta ADE$ is equilateral.

$\therefore\hat{E}=60^{\circ}$, $\hat{D}_1=60^{\circ}$, $\hat{A}_1=60^{\circ}$.

$\therefore\Delta ADE$ is equilateral.
